items.q: A hollow conducting sphere of radius R has charge Q. If the radius is doubled keeping charge same, the electric flux through the Gaussian surface enclosing the sphere will:
items.key: Electric flux depends only on enclosed charge (Gauss's Law: Φ = Q/ε₀), not on size of Gaussian surface.

items.q: Two heaters, each rated 1000 W at 220 V, are connected in parallel across a 220 V supply. Total power consumed is:
items.key: In parallel each heater gets its rated 220 V, so each consumes 1000 W. Total P = 1000 + 1000 = 2000 W.

items.q: A solid metallic cylinder is placed in a uniform magnetic field with its axis parallel to the field. If the field changes with time, the induced (eddy) currents in the cylinder flow:
opts: B. in circular paths around its axis
C. nowhere — no current is induced
D. only along the curved surface, parallel to the axis
items.key: Flux through every circular loop perpendicular to the axis changes, so an emf is induced around such loops. Eddy currents therefore circulate in circles about the axis (Faraday–Lenz).

items.q: An electromagnetic wave propagating along x-axis has equation E = E₀cos(kx−ωt). Direction of propagation is:
items.key: Direction of EM wave propagation is along +x̂ (given by k direction in kx−ωt).

items.q: Which of the following cannot be explained by Huygens' wave theory of light?
items.key: Huygens' principle explains reflection, refraction, interference, diffraction — but NOT origin of spectra (needs quantum theory).

items.q: A distant star sends light to Earth. The wavefront reaching Earth is:
items.key: Star is so far that wavefront is essentially plane by the time it reaches Earth.

items.q: The binding energy per nucleon is maximum for nuclei near iron (Fe-56). This means these nuclei:
opts: D. cannot participate in nuclear reactions
items.key: Maximum binding energy per nucleon = maximum stability = most tightly bound nuclei.

items.q: A small bismuth rod is suspended freely between the poles of a strong electromagnet that produces a non-uniform field. The rod will:
opts: A. align along the field and move towards the stronger field
B. not be affected at all
D. align perpendicular to the field and move towards the weaker field
items.key: Bismuth is diamagnetic (χ small and negative): it is weakly repelled, so it settles across the field and tends to move from stronger to weaker field regions.

items.q: In a Wheatstone bridge, arms AB = 2 Ω, BC = 4 Ω, AD = 3 Ω and DC = 6 Ω. A 5 Ω galvanometer is connected between B and D and an 18 V battery of negligible internal resistance between A and C. Current drawn from the battery is:
items.key: AB/BC = 2/4 = AD/DC = 3/6 → bridge balanced, no current through galvanometer. R_AC = (2+4)(3+6)/(6+9) = 54/15 = 3.6 Ω. I = 18/3.6 = 5 A.

items.q: Resistances R₁ and R₂ dissipate power P₁=60W and P₂=100W from same supply. R₁:R₂ =
items.key: R = V²/P, so R₁/R₂ = P₂/P₁ = 100/60 = 5:3.

items.q: The size of a nucleus is about 10⁻¹⁵ m. If a football (22 cm radius) represents the nucleus, size of atom would be:
items.key: Atom/nucleus ratio ~10⁵. 0.22 m × 10⁵ = 22,000 m = 22 km.

items.q: A circular loop of radius 0.1 m carries current 5 A. Magnetic field at centre:
[A-R Q13] A: Most of the α particles pass undeflected through gold foil. R: Most of the space in atom is empty.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true, and R explains A: the atom is mostly empty space with a tiny nucleus, so most α-particles never come close to the nucleus and pass undeflected.

items.q: [A-R Q14] A: A convex lens submerged in water has greater focal length. R: Lens formula uses relative refractive index.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true, R correctly explains A: in water relative μ decreases, so power decreases, focal length increases.

items.q: [A-R Q15] A: In YDSE, decreasing slit separation increases fringe width. R: Fringe width is directly proportional to slit separation.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true (β = λD/d, d↓ → β↑). R is false (β is INVERSELY proportional to d).

items.q: [A-R Q16] A: Net electric field inside a conductor is zero. R: Electrons in a conductor are always stationary.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true for a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium (free charges rearrange until E inside = 0). R is false — free electrons are in constant random thermal motion; there is just no net drift.

items.q: An electric dipole of moment 4×10⁻⁹ C m is placed in a uniform electric field of 5×10⁴ N/C with its axis at 30° to the field. The torque on the dipole is:
A 4 μF capacitor is charged to a potential difference of 50 V. The energy stored in it is:
A uniform metal wire of resistivity ρ and resistance R is cut into two equal halves, and the halves are joined in parallel. The resistivity of the material of the combination is:
items.key: Resistivity depends only on the material and temperature, not on dimensions. (The resistance changes to R/4, but ρ stays the same.)

items.q: A proton and an α-particle enter a uniform magnetic field with the same velocity, perpendicular to the field. The ratio of the radii of their circular paths, r_p : r_α, is:
items.key: r = mv/(qB). For α: m = 4m_p, q = 2e → r_α = (4m_p v)/(2eB) = 2r_p. So r_p : r_α = 1 : 2.

items.q: The magnetic susceptibility of a paramagnetic salt is 2.4×10⁻⁵ at 300 K. Its susceptibility at 200 K will be:
A bar magnet is dropped, north pole downward, along the axis of a horizontal copper ring. While the magnet is approaching the ring, the induced current in the ring, as seen from above, is:
opts: D. clockwise first and then anticlockwise
items.key: By Lenz's law the ring opposes the approaching N pole by making its upper face a north pole; a north face seen from the viewer's side has anticlockwise current.

items.q: A series AC circuit has a resistance of 30 Ω and an inductive reactance of 40 Ω (no capacitor). The power factor of the circuit is:
items.key: Z = √(30² + 40²) = 50 Ω. Power factor cos φ = R/Z = 30/50 = 0.6.

items.q: Which of the following lists electromagnetic radiations in order of increasing wavelength?
opts: B. X-rays, γ-rays, infrared, radio waves
D. ultraviolet, visible, X-rays, radio waves
items.key: Increasing wavelength: γ-rays → X-rays → UV → visible → IR → microwaves → radio waves. Only option A follows this order.

items.q: A concave mirror of focal length 15 cm forms a real image three times the size of the object. The object is placed in front of the mirror at a distance of:
items.key: Real image: m = −v/u = −3 → v = 3u. 1/v + 1/u = 1/f → 4/(3u) = 1/(−15) → u = −20 cm, i.e. 20 cm in front.

items.q: An electron and a proton have the same kinetic energy. Which of them has the larger de Broglie wavelength?
opts: B. both have the same wavelength
D. it depends on the sign of the charge
items.key: λ = h/p = h/√(2mK). For equal K, smaller mass gives larger λ. The electron is ~1836 times lighter, so its λ is larger.

items.q: The ionisation energy of a hydrogen atom in its ground state is 13.6 eV. The energy needed to excite it from n = 1 to n = 3 is:
In a reverse-biased p-n junction diode (below breakdown), the small current that flows is mainly due to:
opts: B. movement of the fixed ions of the depletion region
C. drift of minority carriers across the junction
items.key: Reverse bias raises the barrier and stops majority-carrier diffusion. Only thermally generated minority carriers are swept across by the junction field, giving a tiny (μA) current.

items.q: [A-R Q13] A: Light from two separate sodium lamps does not produce a sustained interference pattern. R: The two lamps emit light of different wavelengths.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true. R is false — both lamps emit the same wavelength (589 nm), but they are independent sources whose phase difference changes randomly and rapidly, so they are not coherent.

items.q: [A-R Q14] A: The mass of a nucleus is always less than the sum of the masses of its free nucleons. R: When nucleons combine to form a nucleus, energy equivalent to the mass defect is released.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true and R explains A: binding energy is released on formation (E = Δm c²), so the bound nucleus has less mass than the separate nucleons.

items.q: [A-R Q15] A: Kirchhoff's junction rule is based on conservation of charge. R: Kirchhoff's loop rule is based on conservation of energy.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both statements are true, but R describes the loop rule and does not explain the junction rule in A.

items.q: [A-R Q16] A: A ray of light passing through the optical centre of a thin lens suffers a large deviation. R: Near the optical centre the two faces of a thin lens are nearly parallel, like a thin glass slab.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is false — a ray through the optical centre goes undeviated (only a negligible lateral shift). R is true and is the reason for this.

items.q: Two point charges in air repel each other with a force F. If the space between them is filled with a medium of dielectric constant 4 and the distance between them is halved, the force becomes:
A 6 μF capacitor charged to 100 V is connected across an uncharged 3 μF capacitor. The common potential after charge sharing is:
items.key: Charge is conserved: V = C₁V₁/(C₁ + C₂) = (6 × 100)/9 ≈ 66.7 V.

items.q: The I–V graphs of the same metallic wire are drawn at two temperatures T₁ and T₂. Both are straight lines through the origin, and the line for T₁ is steeper (larger slope, I on y-axis). Then:
opts: A. T₁ is higher than T₂
C. T₁ is lower than T₂
D. the temperatures cannot be compared
items.key: Slope of I–V graph = 1/R. Steeper line → smaller R. Resistance of a metal increases with temperature, so T₁ is the lower temperature.

items.q: A circular coil of 20 turns and radius 5 cm carries a current of 1.5 A. The magnitude of its magnetic dipole moment is about:
The net magnetic flux through any closed surface placed in a magnetic field is:
opts: D. μ₀ times the pole strength enclosed
items.key: Gauss's law for magnetism: ∮B·dS = 0. Magnetic field lines form closed loops and isolated magnetic poles (monopoles) do not exist.

items.q: A coil of inductance 50 mH carries a steady current of 4 A. The energy stored in its magnetic field is:
The reactance of a capacitor is 200 Ω at 50 Hz. At 200 Hz its reactance will be:
items.key: X_C = 1/(2πfC) ∝ 1/f. Frequency becomes 4 times → X_C = 200/4 = 50 Ω.

items.q: Displacement current exists in the gap between the plates of a capacitor:
opts: A. only when the capacitor is fully charged
B. only while the electric field between the plates is changing
C. always, even with steady DC after charging
D. only if a dielectric is placed between the plates
items.key: I_d = ε₀ dΦ_E/dt. It is non-zero only while the electric flux (field) between the plates changes, i.e. during charging/discharging or with AC.

items.q: A coin lies at the bottom of a tank filled with water (μ = 4/3) to a depth of 24 cm. When viewed from directly above, the coin appears to be raised by:
items.key: Apparent depth = real depth/μ = 24 × 3/4 = 18 cm. Apparent rise = 24 − 18 = 6 cm.

items.q: The energy of a photon of wavelength 620 nm is about:
items.key: E = hc/λ ≈ 1240 eV nm/620 nm = 2.0 eV.

items.q: The ratio of the nuclear densities of ¹²C and ²⁰⁸Pb is approximately:
items.key: R = R₀A^(1/3) → volume ∝ A, and mass ∝ A, so density is independent of A. Nuclear density is the same (~2.3×10¹⁷ kg/m³) for all nuclei.

items.q: At absolute zero (0 K), a crystal of pure silicon behaves as:
items.key: At 0 K no electron has thermal energy to cross the band gap; the valence band is full and the conduction band empty, so there are no free carriers.

items.q: [A-R Q13] A: In Bohr's model, an electron in a stationary orbit does not radiate energy. R: The angular momentum of the electron in a stationary orbit is an integral multiple of h/2π.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both are true postulates of Bohr's model, but they are separate postulates; quantisation of angular momentum (R) does not explain why the orbit is non-radiating (A).

items.q: [A-R Q14] A: Diffraction of sound is noticed easily in daily life, but diffraction of light is not. R: The wavelength of sound is comparable to the size of everyday obstacles and openings, while the wavelength of light is very much smaller.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true and R explains A: diffraction is appreciable only when the obstacle/aperture size is comparable to the wavelength.

items.q: [A-R Q15] A: The electrostatic potential inside a charged hollow conducting sphere is zero. R: The electric field inside a charged hollow conducting sphere is zero.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is false — since E = 0 inside, the potential is constant inside and equal to its value at the surface, kQ/R (not zero). R is true.

items.q: [A-R Q16] A: Microwaves are used in RADAR systems for aircraft navigation. R: Microwaves have very long wavelengths, so they bend easily around obstacles.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true. R is false — microwaves have short wavelengths (mm to cm), so they travel as narrow, straight beams; that is why they suit RADAR.

items.q: A charge of 3 μC is carried from one point to another on an equipotential surface that is at a potential of 50 V. The work done by the electric field is:
opts: C. 1.5×10⁻⁴ J only if the path is straight
items.key: On an equipotential surface ΔV = 0, so W = qΔV = 0, whatever the path. (The value 50 V of the surface does not matter, only the potential difference.)

items.q: A parallel plate air capacitor stays connected to a battery while a slab of dielectric constant K completely fills the space between its plates. The charge on the capacitor:
items.key: With the battery connected, V stays fixed. C becomes KC₀, so Q = CV = KC₀V = K times the original charge.

items.q: A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω supplies a current of 4 A to an external circuit. The potential difference across its terminals is:
items.key: V = E − Ir = 12 − 4 × 0.5 = 10 V (the cell is discharging, so V is less than E).

items.q: A copper wire is connected across a battery of constant potential difference. If it is replaced by another copper wire of double the length (same thickness and temperature), the drift velocity of the free electrons becomes:
items.key: v_d = eEτ/m and E = V/l. With V fixed and l doubled, E is halved, so v_d is halved.

items.q: A toroid with 400 turns has a mean radius of 10 cm and carries a current of 0.5 A. The magnetic field inside its core (air) is:
A charged particle moves through a region with only a uniform magnetic field. Which quantity of the particle remains constant?
items.key: The magnetic force q(v × B) is always perpendicular to v, so it does no work: the speed and hence kinetic energy stay constant, though the direction of velocity (and momentum) changes.

items.q: The current in a coil of self-inductance 0.3 H falls uniformly from 5 A to 1 A in 0.2 s. The magnitude of the self-induced emf is:
The instantaneous voltage of the household supply is v = 311 sin(100πt) volt. Its rms value and frequency are:
In a plane electromagnetic wave in vacuum, the amplitude of the electric field is 60 V/m. The amplitude of the magnetic field is:
When a narrow beam of white light passes through a glass prism, the colour that is deviated the least is:
items.key: Refractive index of glass is least for red (longest wavelength), and deviation increases with refractive index, so red deviates least.

items.q: A convex lens of focal length 15 cm is used to form a real image of an object on a screen. The minimum possible distance between the object and its real image is:
items.key: For a real image the object–image distance u + v is least when u = v = 2f. Minimum distance = 4f = 4 × 15 = 60 cm.

items.q: The work function of a metal is 3.1 eV. The threshold (longest) wavelength of light that can eject photoelectrons from it is about:
items.key: λ₀ = hc/φ₀ ≈ 1240 eV nm/3.1 eV = 400 nm.

items.q: [A-R Q13] A: In a hydrogen atom, the energy levels come closer and closer together as the principal quantum number n increases. R: The radius of the nth orbit is proportional to n².
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true. A follows from E_n = −13.6/n² eV (the gap between successive levels falls as n grows). R is a correct statement about orbit radii but does not explain the spacing of energy levels.

items.q: [A-R Q14] A: At room temperature, pure germanium conducts better than pure silicon. R: The band gap of germanium (about 0.7 eV) is smaller than that of silicon (about 1.1 eV).
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true and R explains A: with a smaller band gap, many more electrons are thermally excited into the conduction band of Ge, giving more electron–hole pairs and higher conductivity.

items.q: [A-R Q15] A: Total internal reflection can take place when light travels from water into glass. R: For total internal reflection, light must travel from an optically denser medium to an optically rarer medium.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is false — glass is optically denser than water, so light going from water to glass cannot be totally reflected. R is true and is the very reason A fails.

items.q: [A-R Q16] A: Nuclear forces are short-range forces. R: The nuclear force between two nucleons is attractive at all separations.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true — the nuclear force is negligible beyond a few femtometres. R is false — the force is strongly repulsive when nucleons come closer than about 0.8 fm, and attractive only over a small range.

items.q: Two electric field lines never cross each other because:
opts: A. field lines are always straight
C. at any point the electric field has only one direction
D. field lines start only from positive charges
items.key: If two lines crossed, there would be two tangents (two directions of E) at the crossing point, which is impossible since the net field at a point is unique.

items.q: A point charge of 2 nC is fixed in air. The work needed to bring a charge of 3 μC from infinity to a point 30 cm from it is:
Five identical resistors, each of resistance R, are first connected in series and then in parallel. The ratio of the equivalent resistance in series to that in parallel is:
items.key: R_series = 5R, R_parallel = R/5. Ratio = 5R ÷ (R/5) = 25 : 1.

items.q: When the temperature of a metallic conductor is increased, the average relaxation time of its free electrons:
opts: D. first increases and then decreases
items.key: At higher temperature the ions vibrate more strongly, so electrons collide more often; τ decreases, and resistivity ρ = m/(ne²τ) increases.

items.q: A charged particle moves in a circle perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. If its speed is doubled, the time it takes to complete one revolution:
items.key: T = 2πm/(qB), independent of speed. Doubling v doubles the radius r = mv/(qB), but the period is unchanged.

items.q: When a ferromagnetic material such as iron is heated above its Curie temperature, it:
items.key: Above the Curie temperature thermal agitation destroys the alignment of the domains, and the material behaves as a paramagnetic substance.

items.q: A metal rod 1 m long rotates at 10 rad/s about an axis through one end, perpendicular to the rod, in a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T parallel to the axis. The emf induced between its ends is:
An inductor of 10 mH and a capacitor of 1 μF are connected in series to an AC source. The angular frequency at which resonance occurs is:
Many household water purifiers in India use a lamp that kills bacteria in the water. The electromagnetic radiation emitted by this lamp is:
items.key: UV radiation (short wavelength, high-energy photons) damages the DNA of micro-organisms, so UV lamps are used to disinfect drinking water.

items.q: A real object is placed anywhere in front of a convex mirror. The image formed is always:
opts: C. real, erect and of the same size
items.key: For a convex mirror, f is positive and v always comes out positive and smaller than |u|, so the image is behind the mirror (virtual), erect and diminished.

items.q: A thin glass lens (μ = 1.5) is completely immersed in a transparent liquid that also has refractive index 1.5. Inside the liquid the lens:
opts: A. behaves like a plane glass sheet (zero power)
B. has the same focal length as in air
C. has its focal length doubled
D. changes from converging to diverging
items.key: Lens maker's formula: 1/f = (μ_g/μ_l − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂) = (1 − 1)(…) = 0. So f is infinite and the power is zero — the lens becomes practically invisible.

items.q: In a Young's double-slit experiment, the intensity of light from one slit is four times that from the other. The ratio of maximum to minimum intensity in the interference pattern is:
items.key: Amplitudes are in the ratio √4 : 1 = 2 : 1. I_max/I_min = (2 + 1)²/(2 − 1)² = 9 : 1.

items.q: [A-R Q13] A: According to Bohr's model, the electron in a hydrogen atom moves faster in an inner orbit than in an outer orbit. R: The speed of the electron in the nth orbit is inversely proportional to n.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true and R explains A: v_n = e²/(2ε₀nh) ∝ 1/n, so the speed is greatest in n = 1 and decreases outwards.

items.q: [A-R Q14] A: For light above the threshold frequency, the photoelectric current increases when the intensity of light is increased. R: The stopping potential increases when the intensity of light is increased.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true — more photons per second eject more electrons. R is false — the stopping potential depends only on the frequency of light (and the metal), not on intensity.

items.q: [A-R Q15] A: When a p-n junction is formed, holes diffuse from the n-side to the p-side. R: The concentration of holes is much higher on the p-side than on the n-side.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is false — holes diffuse from the p-side (high concentration) to the n-side (low concentration). R is true and shows why the direction in A is wrong.

items.q: [A-R Q16] A: The binding energy per nucleon is nearly the same for nuclei with mass numbers between about 30 and 170. R: The nuclear force between two nucleons is independent of their charge.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both statements are true, but the near-constancy of BE/A is explained by the short range (saturation) of the nuclear force — each nucleon interacts only with its nearest neighbours — not by its charge independence.

items.q: Three equal point charges +q are fixed at the three vertices of an equilateral triangle. The net electric field at the centroid of the triangle is:
opts: C. kq/r², directed away from one vertex
items.key: The three fields at the centroid have equal magnitude (same charge, same distance) and are 120° apart, so their vector sum is zero (superposition).

items.q: The plate area of a parallel plate air capacitor is doubled and, at the same time, the separation between the plates is halved. Its capacitance becomes:
items.key: C = ε₀A/d. New C = ε₀(2A)/(d/2) = 4ε₀A/d = 4C.

items.q: For a cell, the graph of terminal potential difference V (y-axis) against the current I drawn (x-axis) is a straight line that cuts the V-axis at 1.5 V and has a slope of magnitude 0.5 Ω. The current the cell would give if its terminals were short-circuited is:
items.key: V = E − Ir: the intercept is E = 1.5 V and |slope| = r = 0.5 Ω. Short-circuit (V = 0) current = E/r = 1.5/0.5 = 3 A.

items.q: The SI unit of electron mobility is:
items.key: Mobility μ = v_d/E = (m s⁻¹)/(V m⁻¹) = m² V⁻¹ s⁻¹.

items.q: A rectangular loop carrying a steady current is placed in a uniform magnetic field. The loop experiences:
opts: A. a net force but never a torque
B. neither a force nor a torque in any orientation
C. zero net force, but a torque that depends on its orientation
D. a net force and a torque in every orientation
items.key: Forces on opposite sides are equal and opposite, so the net force in a uniform field is zero. They may form a couple: τ = NIAB sin θ, which is zero only when the plane of the loop is perpendicular to B.

items.q: Inside a bar magnet, the magnetic field lines are directed:
opts: A. from the south pole to the north pole
B. from the north pole to the south pole
C. perpendicular to the axis of the magnet
D. nowhere — there is no field inside a magnet
items.key: Magnetic field lines form continuous closed loops: outside the magnet they go from N to S, and inside the magnet they continue from S to N (like the field inside a current-carrying solenoid).

items.q: The henry (H), the SI unit of inductance, is equivalent to:
items.key: Flux linkage Nφ = LI, so L = Nφ/I → 1 H = 1 Wb A⁻¹ (also = 1 V s A⁻¹ from e = L dI/dt).

items.q: For a series LCR circuit at resonance, which one of the following statements is NOT true?
opts: A. The impedance equals the resistance R.
B. The current in the circuit is minimum.
D. The voltages across L and C are equal in magnitude and opposite in phase.
items.key: At resonance X_L = X_C, so Z = R is minimum and the current is MAXIMUM (= V/R). V_L and V_C cancel, current is in phase with voltage and cos φ = 1.

items.q: An electromagnetic wave travels through a non-magnetic medium (μᵣ = 1) whose relative permittivity is 4. Its speed in the medium is:
An astronomical telescope in normal adjustment has a magnifying power of 20, and the distance between its objective and eyepiece is 105 cm. The focal lengths of the objective and the eyepiece are:
items.key: Normal adjustment: f₀ + fₑ = 105 cm and f₀/fₑ = 20 → 21fₑ = 105 → fₑ = 5 cm, f₀ = 100 cm.

items.q: The critical angle for light going from a transparent medium into air is 30°. The refractive index of the medium is:
In a single-slit diffraction experiment with monochromatic light, the slit is made narrower. The central bright band on the screen:
items.key: Angular width of the central maximum = 2λ/a. Reducing the slit width a increases the angular (and linear) width of the central band.

items.q: [A-R Q13] A: For a given frequency and intensity of light, the photoelectric current reaches a saturation value when the collector (anode) potential is made sufficiently positive. R: The stopping potential depends on the frequency of the incident light.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true. A: once all emitted electrons are collected, the current cannot increase further. R is a correct fact about stopping potential but does not explain saturation.

items.q: [A-R Q14] A: The lines of the Lyman series of hydrogen lie in the visible region of the spectrum. R: The Lyman series arises from transitions of the electron from higher levels to the level n = 1.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is false — transitions ending on n = 1 involve large energy gaps (10.2 eV to 13.6 eV), so Lyman lines lie in the ultraviolet. R is true.

items.q: [A-R Q15] A: Isotopes of an element have identical chemical properties. R: Isotopes of an element have the same number of neutrons in their nuclei.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true — chemical properties depend on the number of electrons (= Z), which isotopes share. R is false — isotopes have the same number of protons but DIFFERENT numbers of neutrons.

items.q: [A-R Q16] A: In a crystalline solid, electrons occupy energy bands instead of the sharp energy levels of an isolated atom. R: In a crystal the atoms are so close that the outer electrons of neighbouring atoms interact, and each atomic level splits into a very large number of closely spaced levels.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true and R explains A: the interaction of about 10²³ closely packed atoms splits each level into that many levels, so close together that they form a nearly continuous band.

items.q: Which of the following CANNOT be the charge on an isolated body?
items.key: Charge is quantised: q = ne with n an integer. 2.4×10⁻¹⁹/1.6×10⁻¹⁹ = 1.5, not an integer, so it is impossible. The others are e, 2e and 3e.

items.q: The electric potential in a region varies along the x-axis as V = 4x² volt (x in metre). The electric field at x = 1 m is:
items.key: E = −dV/dx = −8x. At x = 1 m, E = −8 V/m, i.e. 8 V/m pointing along −x (towards decreasing potential).

items.q: n identical cells, each of emf E and internal resistance r, are connected in parallel (all positive terminals joined together). The emf and internal resistance of the combination are:
items.key: In parallel the p.d. across the combination is still E, while the n internal resistances are in parallel: r_eq = r/n.

items.q: A family in Nagpur uses a 1.5 kW electric geyser for 2 hours every day. The electrical energy it consumes in a 30-day month is:
items.key: E = P × t = 1.5 kW × (2 h × 30) = 1.5 × 60 = 90 kWh (90 'units' on the electricity bill).

items.q: Two long straight parallel wires carry steady currents in the same direction. The wires:
opts: C. exert no force on each other
D. tend to rotate until they are perpendicular
items.key: The field of one wire at the other, combined with F = I(L × B), gives a force directed towards the first wire: parallel currents attract, antiparallel currents repel.

items.q: A bar magnet is cut into two equal pieces by a cut perpendicular to its axis. Each piece:
opts: A. has only one pole, N or S
C. is a complete magnet with a N and a S pole, with about half the original magnetic moment
D. is a complete magnet with the same magnetic moment as the original
items.key: Isolated poles do not exist; each piece behaves as a smaller magnet (like a shorter solenoid) with both poles. The pole strength stays about the same while the length halves, so the moment m = q_m × 2l is about halved.

items.q: The magnetic flux linked with a single-turn coil varies with time as Φ = (3t² + 2t) mWb, where t is in seconds. The magnitude of the induced emf at t = 2 s is:
A capacitor allows alternating current to flow in a circuit but blocks steady direct current, because:
opts: A. its resistance is very small for DC
B. its reactance 1/(ωC) is infinite for DC (ω = 0) and finite for AC
C. charges jump across the dielectric only when the voltage alternates
D. DC destroys the dielectric between the plates
items.key: X_C = 1/(2πνC). For DC, ν = 0 so X_C → ∞ (no steady current after charging). For AC, the capacitor charges and discharges continuously, so current flows in the circuit.

items.q: An FM radio station broadcasts at a frequency of 100 MHz. The wavelength of its radio waves in air is:
A plano-convex lens is made of glass of refractive index 1.5, and the radius of curvature of its curved surface is 20 cm. Its focal length in air is:
An object is placed 10 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm. The image is:
opts: A. real, inverted, 20 cm in front of the mirror
C. virtual, diminished, 6.7 cm behind the mirror
D. virtual, erect, twice the size, 20 cm behind the mirror
items.key: u = −10 cm, f = −20 cm: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/20 + 1/10 = 1/20 → v = +20 cm (behind the mirror, virtual). m = −v/u = −20/(−10) = +2: erect and twice the size.

items.q: According to the wave theory of light, when light passes from air into glass, its:
opts: A. frequency decreases and speed stays the same
B. speed decreases and frequency stays the same
C. wavelength increases and speed decreases
D. speed increases and wavelength decreases
items.key: Huygens' theory gives v₂ = v₁/μ — light is slower in the denser medium. Frequency is fixed by the source and does not change; the wavelength λ = v/ν therefore decreases.

items.q: [A-R Q13] A: Energy is released when two deuterium nuclei fuse to form a helium nucleus. R: In a fusion reaction the total number of protons decreases.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true — the product has a much higher binding energy per nucleon, and the extra binding energy is released. R is false — charge (number of protons) and number of nucleons are both conserved in a nuclear reaction.

items.q: [A-R Q14] A: Matter waves associated with a moving electron are electromagnetic waves. R: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle of momentum p is λ = h/p.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is false — matter waves are not electromagnetic; they are associated with any moving particle, charged or neutral, and do not need charge to exist. R is true.

items.q: [A-R Q15] A: Rutherford's nuclear model of the atom could not explain the stability of the atom. R: According to classical electromagnetic theory, an electron revolving round the nucleus is accelerated and must radiate energy continuously, so it should spiral into the nucleus.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true and R explains A: an accelerated charge radiates, so the orbit would shrink continuously and the atom would collapse (and give a continuous spectrum). Bohr's postulates were introduced to remove this difficulty.

items.q: [A-R Q16] A: The output of a half-wave rectifier is pulsating direct current. R: In a full-wave rectifier, the frequency of the output ripple is twice the frequency of the input AC.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both statements are true, but R is about the full-wave rectifier and does not explain A. (A is true because current flows in one direction only, during alternate half-cycles.)

items.q: A hemispherical surface of radius R is placed in a uniform electric field E, with the field parallel to the axis of the hemisphere (so the field lines pass through its flat circular face). The electric flux through the curved surface of the hemisphere is:
items.key: The hemisphere with its flat face forms a closed surface with no charge inside, so the total flux is zero. The flux entering through the flat face is πR²E, so the same flux πR²E leaves through the curved surface.

items.q: A thin ring of radius R carries a charge Q spread uniformly over it. At the centre of the ring, the electric field E and the potential V are:
items.key: The fields of diametrically opposite elements cancel, so E = 0. Potential is a scalar: every element is at distance R, so V = kQ/R (k = 1/4πε₀).

items.q: A steady current flows through a metal conductor whose cross-section is wider at one end than at the other. Which quantity has the same value at every cross-section of the conductor?
items.key: By conservation of charge the same charge passes every cross-section per second, so I is the same. J = I/A, v_d = I/(neA) and E = ρJ are all larger where the conductor is narrower.

items.q: Four resistors, each of resistance R, are joined to form the sides of a square ABCD. The equivalent resistance between the diagonally opposite corners A and C is:
items.key: Between A and C there are two paths, A–B–C and A–D–C, each of resistance 2R, in parallel: R_eq = (2R × 2R)/(2R + 2R) = R.

items.q: The magnetic field at the centre of a long current-carrying solenoid is B. The magnetic field at the middle of one of its end faces is about:
items.key: At an end, the solenoid extends on one side only, so only half of the contribution is present: B_end = μ₀nI/2 = B/2.

items.q: A short bar magnet produces a magnetic field B at a point on its equatorial line at distance r from its centre. The magnetic field at a point on its axis at the same distance r is:
items.key: For a short magnet, B_axial = (μ₀/4π)(2m/r³) and B_equatorial = (μ₀/4π)(m/r³), so B_axial = 2B.

items.q: A passenger aircraft with a wingspan of 40 m flies horizontally at 900 km/h over a place where the vertical component of the Earth's magnetic field is 4×10⁻⁵ T. The emf induced between the tips of its wings is:
items.key: v = 900 km/h = 250 m/s. Only the vertical component is cut by the horizontal wings: e = B_v l v = 4×10⁻⁵ × 40 × 250 = 0.4 V.

items.q: An ideal inductor (zero resistance) is connected to an AC source. The average power consumed by the inductor over one complete cycle is:
items.key: The current lags the voltage by 90°, so P = V_rms I_rms cos 90° = 0. Energy stored in the magnetic field in one quarter-cycle is returned to the source in the next (wattless current).

items.q: Infrared radiation is often called 'heat waves' because:
opts: A. it is emitted only by very hot bodies such as the Sun
B. it travels faster than visible light
C. it is readily absorbed by water molecules and other molecules, increasing their vibrational energy and hence temperature
D. it is produced by the vibration of nuclei
items.key: Infrared frequencies match the vibrational frequencies of many molecules, so it is strongly absorbed and raises the internal energy (temperature) of the substance. All bodies above 0 K emit it, and all EM waves travel at c in vacuum.

items.q: A ray of light passes through an equilateral glass prism in the position of minimum deviation. Inside the prism, the ray travels:
opts: A. perpendicular to the base of the prism
B. parallel to the base of the prism
D. after total internal reflection at the second face
items.key: At minimum deviation the ray passes symmetrically: r₁ = r₂ = A/2 = 30°. Both faces are inclined at 60° to the base, so a ray making 30° with each normal runs parallel to the base.

items.q: The refractive index of glass is 1.5 and that of water is 4/3 (both with respect to air). The refractive index of glass with respect to water is:
In Young's double-slit experiment with slit separation d, screen distance D and wavelength λ, the distance of the third dark fringe from the central bright fringe is:
items.key: Dark fringes lie at y = (2n − 1)λD/2d. For the third dark fringe n = 3: y = 5λD/2d = 2.5 fringe widths.

items.q: [A-R Q13] A: Emission of photoelectrons begins practically instantaneously (within about 10⁻⁹ s) after light of suitable frequency falls on a metal surface. R: The maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons increases with the intensity of the incident light.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true: a single photon gives all its energy hν to one electron in one collision, so there is no time lag. R is false: K_max = hν − φ₀ depends only on frequency; intensity changes only the number of photoelectrons (the current).

items.q: [A-R Q14] A: Nuclear fusion of light nuclei takes place only at extremely high temperatures, such as those inside the Sun. R: The nuclei must have very large kinetic energies to come close enough, against their Coulomb repulsion, for the short-range nuclear force to act.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true, and R explains A: both nuclei are positively charged, so only at temperatures of about 10⁷ K do they have enough thermal kinetic energy to overcome the Coulomb barrier and fuse.

items.q: [A-R Q15] A: An n-type semiconductor is electrically neutral. R: In an n-type semiconductor, free electrons are the majority charge carriers.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true but R does not explain A. Neutrality holds because each free electron given by a pentavalent donor leaves behind a fixed positive donor ion, so total positive and negative charges are equal. R only tells us which carrier is more numerous.

items.q: [A-R Q16] A: In a hydrogen atom, the photon emitted in the transition n = 3 → n = 2 has a shorter wavelength than the photon emitted in the transition n = 2 → n = 1. R: The energy gap between the levels n = 3 and n = 2 is smaller than that between n = 2 and n = 1.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: R is true: E₃ − E₂ = 1.89 eV while E₂ − E₁ = 10.2 eV. Since λ = hc/ΔE, the 3 → 2 photon (656 nm) has a LONGER wavelength than the 2 → 1 photon (122 nm), so A is false.

items.q: The magnitude of the electric field produced by an infinitely long, uniformly charged straight wire at a distance r from it varies as:
items.key: Gauss's law with a coaxial cylinder: E(2πrl) = λl/ε₀ → E = λ/(2πε₀r), so E ∝ 1/r.

items.q: Capacitors of 2 μF and 3 μF are connected in series across a 100 V supply. The charge on each capacitor is:
opts: A. 200 μC on the 2 μF and 300 μC on the 3 μF
items.key: In series both capacitors carry the same charge. C = (2 × 3)/(2 + 3) = 1.2 μF; Q = CV = 1.2 μF × 100 V = 120 μC.

items.q: The resistivity of a metallic wire depends on:
opts: A. the material of the wire and its temperature only
B. its length and area of cross-section
C. its length, area of cross-section and material
D. the current flowing through it
items.key: Resistivity ρ = m/(ne²τ) is a property of the material (n, τ) and changes with temperature; it does not depend on the dimensions of the wire or on the current. Resistance R = ρl/A depends on the dimensions.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT obey Ohm's law?
opts: A. A manganin wire kept at constant temperature
B. A copper wire kept at constant temperature
D. A nichrome wire kept at constant temperature
items.key: For metallic conductors at constant temperature V ∝ I (straight-line V–I graph). A p-n junction diode has a non-linear V–I graph and conducts very differently in the two directions, so it is a non-ohmic device.

items.q: A long straight wire lies along the y-axis and carries a current in the +y direction. The magnetic field it produces at a point on the positive x-axis is directed along:
items.key: By the Biot–Savart law the direction is that of dl × r̂ = ŷ × x̂ = −ẑ (right-hand rule: thumb along +y, fingers curl into the page at points on +x).

items.q: A superconductor placed in a magnetic field expels the field completely from its interior (Meissner effect). Its magnetic susceptibility is:
items.key: Complete expulsion means B = μ₀(1 + χ)H = 0 inside, so χ = −1: a superconductor is a perfect diamagnet.

items.q: The mutual inductance of a pair of coils does NOT depend on:
opts: A. the currents flowing in the coils
B. the distance between the coils
C. the relative orientation of the coils
D. the material of the core on which they are wound
items.key: M depends only on geometry (number of turns, areas, separation, orientation) and on the permeability of the medium. Φ₂ = MI₁, so M is the same whatever the current.

items.q: In a series LCR circuit connected to an AC source, the rms voltages across the inductor, the capacitor and the resistor are 150 V, 150 V and 100 V respectively. The rms voltage of the source is:
items.key: V_L and V_C are 180° out of phase: V = √[V_R² + (V_L − V_C)²] = √(100² + 0) = 100 V. The circuit is at resonance.

items.q: Electromagnetic waves are produced by:
opts: C. charges moving with constant velocity
items.key: A charge at rest produces only an electric field and a steady current only a steady magnetic field. An accelerated (e.g. oscillating) charge produces changing E and B fields that regenerate each other and travel as an EM wave.

items.q: A concave mirror has a focal length of 20 cm in air. When the mirror is completely immersed in water (μ = 4/3), its focal length becomes:
items.key: For a mirror f = R/2 depends only on the radius of curvature; reflection does not depend on the surrounding medium. (A lens's focal length, by contrast, does change.)

items.q: The critical angle for light travelling from glass (μ = 1.5) into water (μ = 4/3) is about:
items.key: sin C = μ_w/μ_g = (4/3)/1.5 = 8/9 ≈ 0.889 → C ≈ 62.7°. (41.8° is the glass–air value, 48.6° the water–air value.)

items.q: In Young's double-slit experiment, one of the two slits is completely covered with an opaque sheet. On the screen:
opts: A. the fringes remain the same, only less bright
C. the interference fringes disappear and only the broad diffraction pattern of a single slit is seen
D. the screen becomes completely dark
items.key: Interference needs two coherent sources. With one slit covered, light from the remaining slit alone gives a single-slit diffraction pattern: a broad bright central region with weak side bands.

items.q: [A-R Q13] A: A proton and an electron moving with the same speed have different de Broglie wavelengths, the proton's being much smaller. R: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle is λ = h/mv, so for the same speed it is inversely proportional to the mass.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true and R explains A: m_p ≈ 1836 m_e, so for equal v the proton's wavelength is about 1/1836 of the electron's.

items.q: [A-R Q14] A: The energy of a hydrogen atom is taken as zero when the electron is in the state n = ∞. R: According to Bohr's model, the radius of the nth orbit is proportional to n².
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true but R does not explain A. A is true because n = ∞ means the electron is free of the nucleus (just ionised) and at rest, which is chosen as the zero of energy (Eₙ = −13.6/n² eV → 0). R is a separate result of Bohr's model.

items.q: [A-R Q15] A: The density of nuclear matter is enormously greater than that of ordinary matter. R: The radius of a nucleus is directly proportional to its mass number A.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true (about 2.3×10¹⁷ kg/m³). R is false: R = R₀A^(1/3), so the volume ∝ A and the nuclear density is the same for all nuclei.

items.q: [A-R Q16] A: A p-type semiconductor carries a net positive charge. R: In a p-type semiconductor, holes are the majority charge carriers.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: R is true. A is false: each hole created by a trivalent acceptor is matched by a fixed negative acceptor ion, so the p-type crystal as a whole is electrically neutral.

items.q: An electric dipole is placed in a non-uniform electric field. In general, it experiences:
opts: A. only a torque, but no net force
B. neither a net force nor a torque
C. only a net force, but never a torque
D. a net force and, in general, a torque as well
items.key: In a non-uniform field the forces qE on the two charges are unequal, so the net force is not zero; unless the dipole is aligned with the field, the two forces also form a couple, giving a torque. (In a uniform field: torque only, no net force.)

items.q: A parallel plate air capacitor of capacitance C₀ has plate separation d. A metal plate of thickness d/2, with the same area as the plates, is slid in between the plates, parallel to them. The new capacitance is:
items.key: There is no field inside the metal, so the effective air gap becomes d − d/2 = d/2. C = ε₀A/(d/2) = 2C₀ (the position of the plate inside the gap does not matter).

items.q: The potential difference across a metallic wire is kept constant, and the wire is replaced by another wire of the same material and cross-section but twice the length. The drift speed of the free electrons:
items.key: v_d = eEτ/m = eVτ/(ml). With V fixed, doubling l halves the electric field inside the wire, so the drift speed is halved.

items.q: A cell of emf E and internal resistance r is connected to an external resistance R. The power delivered to R is maximum when:
opts: D. R is very large compared with r
items.key: P = E²R/(R + r)². Setting dP/dR = 0 gives (R + r) − 2R = 0, i.e. R = r; then P_max = E²/4r.

items.q: An electron moves along the +x direction and enters a region of uniform magnetic field directed along the +y direction. The magnetic force on the electron at that instant is along:
items.key: F = q(v × B) with q = −e. v × B is along î × ĵ = k̂ (+z); multiplying by the negative charge reverses it, so F is along −z.

items.q: Which one of the following statements about magnetic field lines is correct?
opts: A. They begin at the north pole and end at the south pole of a magnet
B. Two field lines can cross each other at a neutral point
C. They form continuous closed loops
D. The tangent to a field line gives the direction of the force on a moving charge
items.key: Since there are no isolated magnetic poles (net flux through any closed surface is zero), magnetic field lines have no start or end: they are closed loops, running N → S outside and S → N inside the magnet. They never cross, and the force on a moving charge is perpendicular to B, not along it.

items.q: Energy loss due to eddy currents in the core of a transformer is reduced by:
opts: A. using a thick solid iron core
B. using a core made of copper
C. operating the transformer at a much higher frequency
D. making the core of thin laminated sheets insulated from each other
items.key: Eddy currents circulate in the plane perpendicular to the changing flux. Thin, insulated laminations break these current paths and increase their resistance, so the eddy currents and the I²R heating in the core fall sharply.

items.q: In a series LCR circuit connected to an AC source, the resistance is 50 Ω and the impedance is 100 Ω. The phase difference between the voltage and the current is:
items.key: Power factor cos φ = R/Z = 50/100 = 0.5, so φ = 60°.

items.q: For a plane electromagnetic wave travelling in vacuum, the ratio of the average energy density associated with the electric field to that associated with the magnetic field is:
items.key: u_E = ½ε₀E² and u_B = B²/2μ₀. With E = cB and c² = 1/(μ₀ε₀): u_E = ½ε₀c²B² = B²/2μ₀ = u_B. The energy is shared equally.

items.q: A concave mirror and a thin convex glass lens each have a focal length of 20 cm for yellow light. For violet light:
opts: A. the focal lengths of both decrease
B. the focal length of the mirror is unchanged, while that of the lens decreases
C. the focal length of the mirror decreases, while that of the lens is unchanged
D. the focal lengths of both remain unchanged
items.key: A mirror's focal length f = R/2 depends only on its geometry, not on wavelength. For the lens 1/f = (μ − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂), and glass has a larger μ for violet than for yellow, so the lens's focal length decreases.

items.q: An object is placed at the focus of a concave lens of focal length 20 cm. The image formed is:
opts: B. real and inverted, 20 cm from the lens on the other side
C. virtual and twice the size of the object, 40 cm from the lens
D. virtual, erect and half the size of the object, 10 cm from the lens on the same side as the object
items.key: 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = −1/20 − 1/20 = −1/10 → v = −10 cm (virtual, same side as the object). m = v/u = (−10)/(−20) = +½: erect and half the size.

items.q: In Young's double-slit experiment, monochromatic light is replaced by white light. The central fringe on the screen is:
items.key: At the centre the path difference is zero for every wavelength, so all colours interfere constructively and the central fringe is white. On either side a few coloured fringes appear (violet edge nearest the centre), and then the pattern fades into uniform illumination.

items.q: [A-R Q13] A: For a given metal, the stopping potential increases when the frequency of the incident light is increased. R: The maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons depends on the intensity of the incident light.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true: eV₀ = hν − φ₀, so V₀ rises linearly with ν. R is false: the maximum kinetic energy depends only on the frequency; a higher intensity gives more photoelectrons (larger current), not faster ones.

items.q: [A-R Q14] A: The emission spectrum of atomic hydrogen consists of sharp, discrete lines. R: The electron in a hydrogen atom can have only certain discrete values of energy.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true. A photon is emitted only in a jump between two allowed levels, with hν = E_i − E_f; since the levels are discrete, only definite frequencies (lines) appear. R correctly explains A.

items.q: [A-R Q15] A: Heavy stable nuclei such as ²⁰⁸Pb contain many more neutrons than protons. R: The nuclear force between two neutrons is much stronger than that between two protons.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true (²⁰⁸Pb has 126 neutrons and 82 protons). R is false: the nuclear force is nearly charge-independent (n–n ≈ p–p ≈ n–p). The extra neutrons add attractive nuclear force without adding Coulomb repulsion, which grows rapidly with the number of protons.

items.q: [A-R Q16] A: The electrical conductivity of an intrinsic semiconductor at room temperature is very small compared with that of a metal. R: At room temperature, only a very small fraction of the valence electrons have enough thermal energy to cross the band gap into the conduction band.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true. With a band gap of about 1 eV, only about 10¹⁶ carriers per m³ are thermally generated in silicon at 300 K, against about 10²⁸ free electrons per m³ in a metal. R correctly explains A.

items.q: Two equal point charges +Q are fixed a distance d apart. A third charge q is placed at the midpoint of the line joining them. For the whole system of three charges to be in equilibrium, q must be:
items.key: The middle charge is in equilibrium for any q. For an end charge: kQ²/d² + kQq/(d/2)² = 0 → Q + 4q = 0 → q = −Q/4.

items.q: Three identical capacitors of 3 μF each are available. To obtain an equivalent capacitance of 4.5 μF, they should be connected:
opts: C. two in parallel, and this pair in series with the third
D. two in series, and this pair in parallel with the third
items.key: Two 3 μF in series give 1.5 μF; adding 3 μF in parallel gives 4.5 μF. (All series: 1 μF; all parallel: 9 μF; option C: 6 μF in series with 3 μF = 2 μF.)

items.q: A steady current flows through a cylindrical wire. If the wire is replaced by one of half the diameter carrying the same current, the current density becomes:
items.key: J = I/A = I/(πd²/4). Halving the diameter makes the area one-fourth, so J becomes four times.

items.q: A uniform wire of resistance 16 Ω is bent into a circle. The resistance between two diametrically opposite points of the circle is:
items.key: The two semicircles, each of 8 Ω, are in parallel between the points: R = (8 × 8)/(8 + 8) = 4 Ω.

items.q: Which one of the following changes will NOT increase the current sensitivity of a moving-coil galvanometer?
opts: A. Increasing the number of turns of the coil
B. Increasing the area of the coil
C. Using a stronger radial magnetic field
D. Using a suspension with a larger torsional constant
items.key: Current sensitivity φ/I = NAB/k. It increases with N, A and B, but decreases if the torsional constant k of the suspension is increased.

items.q: The SI unit of magnetic dipole moment is:
items.key: For a current loop m = NIA, so the unit is ampere × metre² (A m²), which is the same as J/T.

items.q: A closed rectangular conducting loop is moved with a constant velocity through a region of uniform magnetic field perpendicular to its plane, staying completely inside the field region throughout. The emf induced in the loop is:
opts: D. equal to B × (area of loop) × (speed)
items.key: The magnetic flux through the loop stays the same (B and the area inside the field do not change), so dΦ/dt = 0 and no net emf is induced around the loop.

items.q: For an ideal step-up transformer, which of the following quantities is the same for the primary and the secondary coils?
items.key: A transformer changes voltage and current (in opposite ratios) by having different numbers of turns, but the induced emf alternates at the same rate as the flux, so the frequency is unchanged.

items.q: The approximate frequency range of visible light is:
items.key: Visible wavelengths are about 400–750 nm. ν = c/λ gives 3×10⁸/750×10⁻⁹ = 4×10¹⁴ Hz to 3×10⁸/400×10⁻⁹ = 7.5×10¹⁴ Hz.

items.q: The magnifying power of a compound microscope is large when:
opts: A. both the objective and the eyepiece have short focal lengths
B. the objective has a long focal length and the eyepiece a short one
C. both the objective and the eyepiece have long focal lengths
D. the objective has a short focal length and the eyepiece a long one
items.key: M ≈ (L/f_o)(D/f_e), so M is large when both f_o and f_e are small.

items.q: A fish at the bottom of a still pond (refractive index of water 4/3) looks up and sees the whole world above the water through a circular 'window' on the surface. The half-angle of the cone of light that forms this window is about:
items.key: Light from above that grazes the surface (90° in air) is refracted at the critical angle in water: sin C = 1/μ = 3/4 → C ≈ 48.6°. All outside light reaches the fish within this cone.

items.q: In Young's double-slit experiment, the maximum intensity on the screen is I_max. At a point where the path difference between the two waves is λ/4, the intensity is:
items.key: Phase difference φ = (2π/λ)(λ/4) = π/2. I = I_max cos²(φ/2) = I_max cos²(π/4) = I_max/2.

items.q: [A-R Q13] A: A photon of blue light carries more energy than a photon of red light. R: In vacuum, blue light and red light travel with the same speed.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true. A follows from E = hν (blue light has a higher frequency). R is true but is not the reason: the photon energy depends on frequency, not on the speed, which is c for all photons in vacuum.

items.q: [A-R Q14] A: In Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom, the angular momentum of the electron in the third orbit is 3h/2π. R: Bohr's quantum condition allows only those orbits for which mvr = nh/2π, where n is the orbit number.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true. Bohr's second postulate L = nh/2π gives L = 3h/2π for n = 3, so R explains A.

items.q: [A-R Q15] A: Energy is released when a nucleus of ⁵⁶Fe splits into two lighter nuclei. R: ⁵⁶Fe has nearly the largest binding energy per nucleon among all nuclei.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: R is true. A is false: since iron-56 is among the most tightly bound nuclei, splitting it into lighter nuclei (with lower binding energy per nucleon) would need energy to be supplied, not release it.

items.q: [A-R Q16] A: Adding a small amount of a suitable impurity to pure silicon increases its conductivity greatly. R: Doping increases the band gap of silicon.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true: each dopant atom supplies a free electron (donor) or a hole (acceptor), raising the carrier density enormously. R is false: doping does not increase the band gap; it introduces donor or acceptor levels inside the gap, close to the bands.

items.q: An EM wave has frequency ν = 10¹⁸ Hz and travels in vacuum. Find: (i) refractive index of medium if speed is 2×10⁸ m/s, (ii) angular frequency ω.
items.ans:
(i) μ = c/v = 3×10⁸/2×10⁸ = 1.5
(ii) ω = 2πν = 2π×10¹⁸ rad/s; frequency corresponds to X-ray range.

items.q: Distinguish between path of free electrons in a conductor (a) with electric field applied, (b) without electric field.
items.ans:
(a) With E-field: electrons drift opposite to E (superimposed on random motion) → net current flows.
(b) Without E-field: purely random thermal motion; no net displacement → no current.

items.q: Two equal positive charges +q are placed at distance d apart. Find potential and work done to bring charge +q from infinity to midpoint.
Relative permeability of a material is 800. Identify type and state any two properties.
items.ans:
Type: Ferromagnetic (μr >> 1).
Properties: (1) Strongly attracted by magnetic field. (2) Can retain magnetism after field removed (hysteresis).

items.q: An AC source with frequency 50 Hz is connected to an inductor. If current lags voltage by 90°, explain why? Find reactance if L = 2 H.
items.ans:
In pure inductor, current lags voltage by 90° due to back-emf opposing change in current.
X_L = 2πfL = 2π×50×2 = 200π ≈ 628 Ω.

items.q: Two point charges +5 μC and −3 μC are placed 40 cm apart in air. Find the points on the line joining them where the electric potential is zero.
items.ans:
Let the point be at distance x from +5 μC. V = k(5/x − 3/r₂) = 0 → 5/x = 3/r₂.
Between the charges (r₂ = 0.40 − x): 5(0.40 − x) = 3x → x = 0.25 m, i.e. 25 cm from +5 μC (15 cm from −3 μC). [1]
Outside, beyond −3 μC (r₂ = x − 0.40): 5(x − 0.40) = 3x → x = 1.0 m, i.e. 60 cm beyond the −3 μC charge. [1]

items.q: A galvanometer of resistance 40 Ω gives full-scale deflection for a current of 2 mA. How will you convert it into a voltmeter of range 0–10 V? What is the resistance of the voltmeter so formed?
items.ans:
Connect a high resistance R in series: R = V/I_g − G = 10/(2×10⁻³) − 40 = 5000 − 40 = 4960 Ω. [1]
Resistance of voltmeter = G + R = 5000 Ω (high, so it draws little current). [1]

items.q: In Young's double-slit experiment, light of wavelength 600 nm is used, the slits are 0.3 mm apart and the screen is 1.5 m away. Find (i) the fringe width, (ii) the distance of the third dark fringe from the central bright fringe.
Light of wavelength 400 nm falls on a metal surface of work function 2.3 eV. Find (i) the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons, (ii) the stopping potential.
Explain how the depletion region and the barrier potential are formed in a p-n junction.
items.ans:
When the junction is formed, electrons diffuse from n-side to p-side and holes from p-side to n-side (concentration difference). They leave behind immobile positive donor ions on the n-side and negative acceptor ions on the p-side near the junction — this layer, free of mobile carriers, is the depletion region. [1]
These ions set up an electric field from n to p that opposes further diffusion and causes drift of minority carriers. At equilibrium diffusion current = drift current; the potential difference across the depletion layer is the barrier potential (≈ 0.7 V for Si, 0.3 V for Ge). [1]

items.q: A point charge of 1.77 μC is placed at the centre of a cube of side 10 cm. Find (i) the total electric flux through the cube, (ii) the flux through one face of the cube. (ε₀ = 8.85×10⁻¹² C² N⁻¹ m⁻²)
items.ans:
(i) By Gauss's law Φ = q/ε₀ = 1.77×10⁻⁶/8.85×10⁻¹² = 2.0×10⁵ N m² C⁻¹ (independent of the cube's size). [1]
(ii) By symmetry each of the 6 faces gets equal flux: Φ_face = 2.0×10⁵/6 ≈ 3.33×10⁴ N m² C⁻¹. [1]

items.q: Pure silicon has an intrinsic carrier concentration of 1.5×10¹⁶ m⁻³. It is doped with arsenic so that the free-electron concentration becomes 3×10²² m⁻³. Find the hole concentration and state the type of semiconductor formed.
items.ans:
n_e n_h = n_i² → n_h = (1.5×10¹⁶)²/(3×10²²) = 2.25×10³²/3×10²² = 7.5×10⁹ m⁻³. [1]
Since n_e ≫ n_h (arsenic is pentavalent, a donor), it is an n-type semiconductor. [1]

items.q: The current in a coil changes steadily from 2 A to 6 A in 0.05 s, and an emf of 0.8 V is induced in a neighbouring coil. Find (i) the mutual inductance of the pair, (ii) the change in flux linkage with the second coil.
A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 30 cm. Find the power and focal length of the combination, and state its nature.
items.ans:
P = P₁ + P₂ = 100/20 + 100/(−30) = 5 − 3.33 ≈ +1.67 D. [1]
f = 1/P = 100/1.67 cm = 60 cm; positive power → the combination behaves as a converging (convex) lens. [1]

items.q: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 150 V. Calculate its de Broglie wavelength. In which region of the electromagnetic spectrum does a photon of this wavelength lie?
items.ans:
λ = h/√(2meV) = 6.63×10⁻³⁴/√(2 × 9.11×10⁻³¹ × 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ × 150) ≈ 1.0×10⁻¹⁰ m (or λ = 1.227/√V nm = 0.100 nm). [1]
λ ≈ 0.1 nm = 1 Å, which lies in the X-ray region (comparable to inter-atomic spacing). [1]

items.q: Two wires A and B are made of the same metal. B is twice as long as A and has twice its diameter. Find the ratio of their resistances. If they are connected in series across a battery, find the ratio of the powers dissipated in A and B.
items.ans:
R = ρl/A = 4ρl/(πd²), so R ∝ l/d². R_B/R_A = 2/2² = 1/2 → R_A : R_B = 2 : 1. [1]
In series the same current flows, so P = I²R ∝ R → P_A : P_B = 2 : 1. [1]

items.q: A straight wire 0.5 m long carrying a current of 3 A is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 0.4 T, the wire making an angle of 30° with the field. Find the force on the wire. At what angle would this force be maximum, and what would be its value?
items.ans:
F = BIl sin θ = 0.4 × 3 × 0.5 × sin 30° = 0.3 N, perpendicular to the plane containing the wire and B (Fleming's left-hand rule). [1]
Maximum when the wire is perpendicular to the field (θ = 90°): F_max = BIl = 0.4 × 3 × 0.5 = 0.6 N. [1]

items.q: A ray of light is incident at 60° on the surface of a glass slab of refractive index √3. Find the angle of refraction and show that the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other.
items.ans:
Snell's law: sin r = sin 60°/√3 = (√3/2)/√3 = 1/2 → r = 30°. [1]
Reflected ray makes 60° with the normal and the refracted ray 30° on the other side, so the angle between them = 180° − 60° − 30° = 90°. [1]

items.q: A proton and an α-particle are each accelerated from rest through the same potential difference. Find the ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths, λ_p : λ_α.
Give two differences between intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors. Why does doping silicon with a trivalent impurity produce a p-type semiconductor?
items.ans:
Intrinsic: pure, n_e = n_h, very low conductivity at room temperature. Extrinsic: doped with impurity, n_e ≠ n_h, much higher and controllable conductivity. [1]
A trivalent atom (B, Al, Ga, In) forms only three covalent bonds with neighbouring Si atoms; the vacancy in the fourth bond is a hole, which can accept an electron. So holes become the majority carriers → p-type. [1]

items.q: An electron is released from rest in a uniform electric field of 2×10⁴ N/C between two charged plates. Find (i) its acceleration, (ii) the time it takes to travel 1.5 cm. (e = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C, m_e = 9.11×10⁻³¹ kg; neglect gravity)

A straight horizontal wire of mass 20 g and length 0.5 m is placed in a uniform horizontal magnetic field of 0.4 T perpendicular to the wire. What current must flow in it so that it stays suspended in mid-air? How should the direction of current be chosen? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
items.ans:
For suspension the magnetic force balances the weight: BIl = mg → I = mg/(Bl) = (0.02 × 9.8)/(0.4 × 0.5) = 0.98 A. [1]
Direction: chosen so that the force IL × B points vertically upward (by Fleming's left-hand rule), e.g. for B pointing north, current must flow from west to east. [1]

items.q: A ray of light falls normally on one face of an equilateral glass prism of refractive index √2. Find the critical angle for glass and trace the path of the ray. Will it emerge from the second face?
items.ans:
Critical angle: sin C = 1/√2 → C = 45°. [1]
The ray enters undeviated (normal incidence) and meets the second face at an angle of incidence equal to the prism angle, 60°. Since 60° is greater than 45°, it is totally internally reflected and does not emerge from the second face; the reflected ray then meets the third face normally and passes out undeviated. [1]

items.q: The total energy of the electron in the ground state of a hydrogen atom is −13.6 eV. (i) What are its kinetic and potential energies in this state? (ii) What is the total energy of the electron in the n = 4 state?
items.ans:
(i) In Bohr's model K = −E and U = 2E: K = +13.6 eV, U = −27.2 eV. [1]
(ii) E₄ = −13.6/4² = −0.85 eV. [1]

items.q: A silicon diode (forward voltage drop 0.7 V) is connected in series with a 220 Ω resistor across a 5 V battery so that it is forward biased. Find the current in the circuit. What will the current be (approximately) if the battery terminals are reversed? Give reason.
items.ans:
Forward bias: I = (5 − 0.7)/220 = 4.3/220 ≈ 0.0195 A ≈ 19.5 mA. [1]
Reversed: the diode is reverse biased and offers very high resistance; only a tiny reverse saturation current (of the order of μA or less) flows, so the current is practically zero. [1]

items.q: Two point charges +4 μC and +1 μC are fixed 30 cm apart in air. Find the position of the point on the line joining them where the net electric field is zero. Is there any other such point at a finite distance?
items.ans:
Let the point be at distance x from +4 μC, between the charges. k(4 μC)/x² = k(1 μC)/(0.30 − x)² → 2(0.30 − x) = x → x = 0.20 m, i.e. 20 cm from +4 μC (10 cm from +1 μC). [1]
No. Outside the charges both fields point the same way (both charges are positive), so they cannot cancel; the only null point is between them, nearer the smaller charge. [1]

items.q: An electron moves with a speed of 2×10⁶ m/s perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 mT. Find (i) the radius of its circular path, (ii) the frequency of revolution. (m_e = 9.11×10⁻³¹ kg, e = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C)

A parallel plate capacitor, with plates of area 0.01 m² in air, is being charged by a current of 0.2 A. Find (i) the displacement current between the plates, (ii) the rate at which the electric field between the plates is changing. (ε₀ = 8.85×10⁻¹² C² N⁻¹ m⁻²)
items.ans:
(i) The displacement current in the gap equals the conduction current in the leads: I_d = 0.2 A (this keeps the current continuous, as Ampere–Maxwell law requires). [1]
(ii) I_d = ε₀ dΦ_E/dt = ε₀A dE/dt → dE/dt = 0.2/(8.85×10⁻¹² × 0.01) ≈ 2.26×10¹² V m⁻¹ s⁻¹. [1]

items.q: Using E = mc², show that the energy equivalent of 1 atomic mass unit is about 931.5 MeV. Also find the energy equivalent of 1 mg of matter in joules. (1 u = 1.6605×10⁻²⁷ kg, c = 2.998×10⁸ m/s, 1 MeV = 1.602×10⁻¹³ J)
items.ans:
E = mc² = 1.6605×10⁻²⁷ × (2.998×10⁸)² ≈ 1.4925×10⁻¹⁰ J = 1.4925×10⁻¹⁰/1.602×10⁻¹³ MeV ≈ 931.5 MeV. [1]
For 1 mg: E = 10⁻⁶ kg × (3×10⁸)² ≈ 9×10¹⁰ J — an enormous energy from a tiny mass. [1]

items.q: The barrier potential of a silicon p-n junction is 0.7 V. What will be the effective height of the potential barrier when (i) a forward bias of 0.3 V is applied, (ii) a reverse bias of 2 V is applied? How does the width of the depletion region change in each case?
items.ans:
(i) Forward bias opposes the barrier: effective barrier = 0.7 − 0.3 = 0.4 V; the depletion region becomes narrower. [1]
(ii) Reverse bias adds to the barrier: effective barrier = 0.7 + 2 = 2.7 V; the depletion region becomes wider. [1]

items.q: Draw (describe) the equipotential surfaces for (a) a uniform electric field, (b) an isolated point charge. Why must equipotential surfaces be perpendicular to the field lines? In a uniform field of 500 V/m, what is the potential difference between two equipotential surfaces 2 cm apart?
items.ans:
(a) Uniform field: parallel equidistant planes perpendicular to the field. (b) Point charge: concentric spheres centred on the charge (closer together near the charge). Since no work is done in moving a charge along an equipotential, E can have no component along the surface, so E is perpendicular to it. [1]
ΔV = Ed = 500 × 0.02 = 10 V. [1]

items.q: The magnetic susceptibility of material A is −2.1×10⁻⁵ and that of material B is +3.7×10⁻⁴. Identify each type of magnetic material and find its relative permeability. How do the magnetic field lines behave when each is placed in a uniform external field?
items.ans:
A: diamagnetic (χ small, negative), μᵣ = 1 + χ ≈ 0.999979. B: paramagnetic (χ small, positive), μᵣ ≈ 1.00037. [1]
Field lines are slightly pushed out of (spread away from) the diamagnetic material A, so the field inside it is slightly weaker; they are slightly drawn into (concentrated in) the paramagnetic material B, so the field inside it is slightly stronger. [1]

items.q: A ray of light is incident on one face of a glass prism of refractive angle 60° and refractive index 1.5. Find the angle of incidence for which the ray just grazes along the second face as it emerges.
items.ans:
For grazing emergence, the angle of incidence at the second face equals the critical angle: sin C = 1/1.5 → C = r₂ ≈ 41.8°. Then r₁ = A − r₂ = 60° − 41.8° = 18.2°. [1]
sin i = μ sin r₁ = 1.5 × sin 18.2° ≈ 0.468 → i ≈ 27.9°. (For any smaller angle of incidence, the ray is totally reflected at the second face.) [1]

items.q: For a photosensitive metal, the graph of stopping potential V₀ (y-axis) against frequency ν of the incident light is a straight line cutting the frequency axis at 5×10¹⁴ Hz. What is the work function of the metal (in eV)? What does the slope of the graph represent, and what is its value? (h = 6.63×10⁻³⁴ J s, e = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C)
items.ans:
Threshold frequency ν₀ = 5×10¹⁴ Hz: φ₀ = hν₀ = 6.63×10⁻³⁴ × 5×10¹⁴ ≈ 3.3×10⁻¹⁹ J ≈ 2.07 eV. [1]
From eV₀ = hν − φ₀, V₀ = (h/e)ν − φ₀/e, so the slope = h/e = 6.63×10⁻³⁴/1.6×10⁻¹⁹ ≈ 4.1×10⁻¹⁵ V s — the same for every metal. [1]

items.q: What is a 'hole' in a semiconductor? Explain how holes move when an electric field is applied, and why the total current in a semiconductor is the sum of electron and hole currents.
items.ans:
When an electron leaves a covalent bond (moving into the conduction band), the vacancy left in the bond behaves like a positive charge +e; this vacancy is a hole. [1]
In an electric field, an electron from a neighbouring bond jumps into the hole, creating a new hole where it came from; so the hole moves in the direction of the field (opposite to the electrons). Free electrons drift against E and holes drift along E, so both carry conventional current in the same direction: I = I_e + I_h. [1]

items.q: An oil drop of mass 3.2×10⁻¹⁵ kg is held stationary between two horizontal metal plates 1.0 cm apart when a potential difference of 1000 V is applied across them. (i) Find the charge on the drop and the number of excess electrons on it. (ii) Which plate, upper or lower, is at the higher potential? (g = 10 m/s², e = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C)
items.ans:
(i) E = V/d = 1000/0.01 = 10⁵ V/m. For balance qE = mg → q = mg/E = (3.2×10⁻¹⁵ × 10)/10⁵ = 3.2×10⁻¹⁹ C; n = q/e = 3.2×10⁻¹⁹/1.6×10⁻¹⁹ = 2 electrons. [1]
(ii) The drop has excess electrons (negative charge), so the electric force must be upward, i.e. the field must point downward — the upper plate is at the higher (positive) potential. [1]

items.q: n identical cells, each of emf E and internal resistance r, are to be connected to an external resistance R that is equal to r. Show that the current through R is the same whether the cells are all joined in series or all joined in parallel.
items.ans:
Series: total emf nE, total internal resistance nr → I_s = nE/(R + nr) = nE/(r + nr) = nE/[r(n + 1)]. [1]
Parallel: emf E, internal resistance r/n → I_p = E/(R + r/n) = E/(r + r/n) = nE/[r(n + 1)]. Hence I_s = I_p when R = r. [1]

items.q: A tall glass jar contains water (μ = 4/3) to a depth of 12 cm, with a 5 cm thick layer of oil (μ = 1.25) floating on it. A coin lies at the bottom. Find the apparent depth of the coin below the oil surface when it is viewed from directly above, and the distance by which the coin appears to be raised.
items.ans:
For near-normal viewing each layer appears shortened by its own refractive index: apparent depth = t₁/μ₁ + t₂/μ₂ = 5/1.25 + 12/(4/3) = 4 + 9 = 13 cm. [1]
Real depth = 5 + 12 = 17 cm, so the coin appears raised by 17 − 13 = 4 cm. [1]

items.q: A laser emits light of wavelength 500 nm. (i) Find the momentum of each photon. (ii) The 2 mW beam falls normally on a black surface that absorbs it completely. Find the force exerted on the surface. (h = 6.63×10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3×10⁸ m/s)
items.ans:
(i) p = h/λ = 6.63×10⁻³⁴/(500×10⁻⁹) ≈ 1.33×10⁻²⁷ kg m/s. [1]
(ii) Each photon has energy E = pc, so the momentum delivered per second = P/c. Force F = P/c = (2×10⁻³)/(3×10⁸) ≈ 6.7×10⁻¹² N. [1]

items.q: Draw (describe) the energy band diagrams of (i) an n-type and (ii) a p-type semiconductor at room temperature, showing the position of the donor or acceptor energy level.
items.ans:
(i) n-type: the donor level E_D lies just below the bottom of the conduction band (about 0.01 eV for Ge, 0.05 eV for Si). At room temperature most donor electrons are excited into the conduction band, so the conduction band has many electrons and the valence band only a few holes. [1]
(ii) p-type: the acceptor level E_A lies just above the top of the valence band. Valence electrons easily jump into the acceptor level, leaving many holes in the valence band; the conduction band has only a few thermally generated electrons. [1]

items.q: A point charge of 8 μC is fixed at the origin in air. Find the work done by an external agent in slowly moving a charge of 2 μC from the point P (3 cm, 0) to the point Q (0, 4 cm). Does the answer depend on the path followed? Explain. (k = 9×10⁹ N m² C⁻²)
items.ans:
V_P = kq/r_P = 9×10⁹ × 8×10⁻⁶/0.03 = 2.4×10⁶ V; V_Q = 9×10⁹ × 8×10⁻⁶/0.04 = 1.8×10⁶ V. W = q(V_Q − V_P) = 2×10⁻⁶ × (1.8 − 2.4)×10⁶ = −1.2 J. [1]
(The agent does −1.2 J of work, i.e. the field does +1.2 J as the charges move apart.) No — the electrostatic force is conservative, so the work depends only on the initial and final positions, not on the path. [1]

items.q: Define one ampere in terms of the force between two parallel current-carrying conductors. Two long straight parallel wires 5 cm apart in air carry currents of 10 A and 15 A in opposite directions. Find the force per metre length on each wire and state whether it is attractive or repulsive. (μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷ T m/A)
items.ans:
One ampere is the steady current which, when maintained in each of two very long, straight, parallel conductors of negligible cross-section placed 1 m apart in vacuum, produces between them a force of 2×10⁻⁷ N per metre of length. [1]
F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd) = 2×10⁻⁷ × 10 × 15/0.05 = 6×10⁻⁴ N/m on each wire; since the currents are opposite, the force is repulsive. [1]

items.q: Draw (describe) the shape of the wavefront in each case: (i) light diverging from a point source, (ii) light emerging from a convex lens when a point source is placed at its focus, (iii) a plane wavefront after reflection from a concave mirror, (iv) a plane wavefront after passing through a thin prism.
items.ans:
(i) Spherical wavefronts, centred on the source and spreading outwards. [½]
(ii) Plane wavefront — the lens makes the emergent rays parallel. [½]
